Technology stocks climbed back to positive territory in recent trading, with the shares of tech stocks in the S&P 500 rising almost 0.8% in value this afternoon while the Philadelphia Semiconductor Index soared nearly 3.6% higher.
Among technology stocks moving on news:
(+) Take-Two Interactive Software ( TTWO ) rose over 12% at one point on Tuesday after its Red Dead Redemption 2 achieved the best-ever opening weekend for an electronic games publisher, pocketing more than $725 million in worldwide retail sell-through during its first three days. Red Dead Redemption 2 also had the second-highest gross entertainment launch of all time, lagging only Grand Theft Auto V, which achieved more than $1 billion in retail sell-through over its first three days on the market.
In other sector news:
(+) Akamai ( AKAM ) climbed over 16% on Tuesday after Suntrust analysts raised their investment rating for the cloud-services company and RBC Capital Markets and B. Riley increase their price target for Akamai shares in response to it reporting above-consensus Q3 financial results and authorizing a new stock buyback program for up to $1.1 billion of its common stock beginning Nov. 1 and running through the end of 2021. Excluding one-time items, the company earned $0.94 per share during the September quarter, rising 47% over its year-ago profit and beating the Capital IQ consensus by $0.11 per share. Revenue rose 7% over the same quarter last year to $669.6 million and edging out the $664.2 million analyst mean.
(+) Sony ( SNE ) advanced almost 8% at one point on Tuesday after reporting better-than-expected fiscal Q2 financial results and boosting its FY19 earnings and sales outlook as well as receiving unconditional approval for its proposed acquisition of EMI Music Publishing from European regulators.
(-) Rambus ( RMBS ) fell to a nearly 16-year low on Tuesday, reaching its lowest share price since November 2002 at $7.30 a share despite the date memory chipmaker reporting better-than-expected Q3 net income and naming Luc Seraphin as its permanent chief executive officer. Seraphin was general manager of the company's largest business unit and had been interim CEO since June.
